CHN.note: FAOSTAT/USDA: China is by far the world's largest egg producer (~29 Mt of hen eggs in shell, roughly 35-40% of global output). Almost all consumed domestically; shell-egg (HS0407) exports are modest and go mainly to Hong Kong and Macau. Shell eggs are a very low-trade-ratio commodity.

USA.note: USDA: the US produces ~6.6 Mt of shell eggs but its flock was hammered by 2022-2025 HPAI (highly pathogenic avian influenza), culling tens of millions of layers. Normally a small net exporter (to Canada, Mexico, Caribbean); turned net importer during the 2025 shortage, importing shell eggs from Turkey and Brazil to ease record retail prices.

IND.note: FAOSTAT: India is the #2-#3 egg producer (~6.4 Mt). Output is overwhelmingly for the domestic market; shell-egg (HS0407) exports are small and go to neighbours (Maldives, Sri Lanka, Gulf, Oman). Imports negligible.

IDN.note: FAOSTAT: Indonesia ~5.5 Mt; a top-five producer. Essentially self-contained — shell eggs are produced and consumed domestically with negligible HS0407 trade either way.

BRA.note: FAOSTAT/USDA: Brazil ~3.2 Mt. Historically domestic-focused, but shell-egg (HS0407) exports rose sharply in 2025 as Brazil supplied the US shortage and Gulf/African buyers. A growing net shell-egg exporter.

MEX.note: FAOSTAT/USDA: Mexico ~3.1 Mt and the world's highest per-capita egg consumer. Mostly self-sufficient but a structural net shell-egg (HS0407) importer from the US along the border, especially when US prices/supply allow.

JPN.note: FAOSTAT: Japan ~2.5 Mt; near self-sufficient in shell eggs. Exports premium/specialty shell eggs (HS0407) to Hong Kong; imports liquid/dried egg products (outside HS0407) for processing. 2022-23 HPAI tightened domestic supply.

RUS.note: FAOSTAT: Russia ~2.6 Mt. Normally self-sufficient, but turned a notable shell-egg (HS0407) net importer in 2024 after price spikes and supply problems, sourcing from Belarus, Turkey, Azerbaijan and Iran; Moscow temporarily zeroed import duties.

NLD.note: FAOSTAT/Comtrade 2024: the Netherlands is the world's #1 shell-egg (HS0407) EXPORTER despite modest output (~0.65 Mt). A trade hub: imports eggs from Germany, Belgium, Poland, Spain, Denmark and re-exports, with Germany the dominant destination (Comtrade DEU import from NLD 268 kt 2024). Strong net exporter.

DEU.note: FAOSTAT/Comtrade 2024: Germany ~0.9 Mt produced vs ~1.2 Mt consumed; the world's largest shell-egg (HS0407) IMPORTER. Buys heavily from the Netherlands (Comtrade 268 kt 2024) and Poland; the cage-ban shift left a structural deficit. Large net importer.

POL.note: FAOSTAT: Poland ~0.7 Mt and a leading EU shell-egg (HS0407) EXPORTER — ships to Germany, Netherlands, Czechia, UK, France. Low-cost layer base makes it a structural net exporter.

ESP.note: FAOSTAT: Spain ~1.0 Mt; a net shell-egg (HS0407) EXPORTER within the EU, supplying France, Netherlands, Portugal and Italy. Competitive producer with surplus capacity.

TUR.note: FAOSTAT/USDA: Turkey ~1.05 Mt and one of the world's biggest shell-egg (HS0407) EXPORTERS — long-standing supplier to Iraq, and in 2025 a key emergency supplier to the United States during the US HPAI shortage. Large net exporter.

BEL.note: FAOSTAT/Comtrade 2024: Belgium is a shell-egg (HS0407) entrepot — imports ~186 kt from the Netherlands (Comtrade 2024) and re-exports into the Benelux/EU loop. Roughly trade-balanced, high turnover relative to small domestic production.

FRA.note: FAOSTAT: France ~0.95 Mt; broadly self-sufficient but a modest net shell-egg (HS0407) importer, sourcing from Spain, Poland, Netherlands and Belgium to top up retail and processing demand.

IRQ.note: FAOSTAT: Iraq is a structural net shell-egg (HS0407) IMPORTER, with Turkey its dominant supplier (seed TUR->IRQ 168 kt). Domestic output falls short of demand.

GBR.note: FAOSTAT/Defra: the UK ~0.6 Mt; a net shell-egg (HS0407) importer, mainly from Poland, the Netherlands, Spain and France, after HPAI and free-range supply pressures tightened domestic availability.

rankings.note: Hen eggs in shell HS0407, 2024, kt. Exporters led by the Netherlands (#1, a re-export hub), Poland, Turkey, then the US/Germany/Spain; China exports mainly to Hong Kong/Macau. Importers led by Germany (#1), the Benelux re-export hubs, the US (2024-25 HPAI shortage), Iraq (Turkish supply) and Hong Kong. Shell eggs are a low-trade-ratio commodity — under ~3% of global production crosses borders, mostly short-haul regional flows. HKG import figure is Comtrade 2024.

companies.name: Cal-Maine Foods
companies.note: Largest shell-egg producer in the United States (~20% of US table-egg sales); NASDAQ-listed, revenue ~US$3-4bn (FY2024-25, lifted by HPAI-driven price spikes). Production is domestic US; it sells into the US market rather than exporting HS0407.
companies.improve: Should disclose flock-by-state and HPAI-loss tonnage; export volumes are negligible and not separately reported.

companies.name: Avril / Matines (Groupe Avril)
companies.note: Major French egg producer/packer (Matines and Ovoteam brands) within agro-industrial Groupe Avril. Supplies the French retail and processing market; France is broadly self-sufficient so volumes are largely domestic.
companies.improve: Private-group reporting bundles eggs with oils/proteins; standalone egg tonnage and any HS0407 exports are not separately published.

companies.name: Interovo Egg Group
companies.note: One of the Netherlands' largest egg packers/traders, central to the Dutch re-export hub that makes NLD the world's #1 shell-egg (HS0407) exporter. Sources eggs across NW Europe and grades/re-exports, chiefly to Germany.
companies.improve: Private; origin-split of sourced eggs and re-export tonnage by destination are not publicly disclosed.

companies.name: Yabani / Keskinoglu
companies.note: Keskinoglu is one of Turkey's largest integrated poultry/egg producers, part of the export base that makes Turkey a top shell-egg (HS0407) exporter to Iraq and, in 2025, an emergency supplier to the US during the HPAI shortage.
companies.improve: Private; egg-segment export tonnage by destination not separately published.

companies.name: Granja Mantiqueira
companies.note: Brazil's largest egg producer (Happy Eggs brand). Historically domestic-focused, it sits behind Brazil's 2025 surge in shell-egg (HS0407) exports to the US and Gulf/African markets.
companies.improve: Private; export volumes are recent and not yet consistently disclosed by destination.

companies.name: Pulmuone / Hy-Line layer genetics
companies.note: Hy-Line International (EW Group / part of the global layer-genetics duopoly with Lohmann) supplies the laying-hen breeding stock behind a large share of the world's egg production. Trades breeding stock/genetics, not shell eggs (HS0407) directly.
companies.improve: Genetics flows (parent stock, hatching eggs) sit outside HS0407 shell-egg statistics and are not captured in this commodity's trade matrix.

global.note: World hen-egg (in shell) totals, kt (FAOSTAT/USDA). Global output ~86-90 Mt and rising steadily; China alone is ~35-40%, with India, Indonesia, the US, Brazil and Mexico the other large producers. World shell-egg (HS0407) exports are only ~2.5 Mt — under 3% of production — because eggs are fragile, perishable and mostly consumed domestically; trade is dominated by short-haul EU (NLD/DEU/POL) and regional Asian/Middle-East flows. 2022-2025 HPAI (avian influenza) caused sharp supply shocks, notably the 2025 US egg shortage that pulled in imports from Turkey and Brazil.
